proof.criterion: A1. The binding names its Role by an output that waits on the Role's ID, so a preview that creates the Role sends the API server no server-side dry run of the binding.
proof.surface: The envoy-infra plugin as a consumer loads it (pulumitest.Construct, which serves provider.New in process and takes the ConstructRequest's DryRun), and the component under the mock engine. Both read on a preview and on an apply.
proof.observed: PASS, four subtests: component/preview=false, component/preview=true, plugin/preview=false, plugin/preview=true. On both surfaces the RoleBinding's roleRef.name is unknown under preview (the mock monitor records an unknown input as null) and resolves to example-dispatch-tailnet-tls on an apply; roleRef.kind is Role in all four.
proof.negativeControl: The same test over the tree this branch started from, abc15e0135a05cec3f94b9fe7d3943aae79ff81c, unpacked with `git archive abc15e01 packages/envoy | tar -x -C $TMPDIR/neg` on the issue's volume with only gcp/dispatch_test.go, gcp/dispatch_construct_test.go and internal/pulumitest/mocks.go copied over it: component/preview=true and plugin/preview=true both FAIL with `roleRef name on a preview = {example-dispatch-tailnet-tls}, want unknown until the Role exists`, the literal name the old code set, while both preview=false cases pass. The plugin surface fails too, so the Construct case is not a vacuous pass.

proof.criterion: A2. The Tailscale Service svc:<hostname> is declared with no tags, and the component's tags input still reaches the front door's nodes.
proof.surface: The component's registrations under the mock engine: the tailscale:index/service:Service the component declares, and the front door's pod, which renders --advertise-tags from the same tags input.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy/infra && go test -count=1 -run 'TestDispatchDeclaresItsTailscaleService|TestDispatchFrontDoorPodHostsTheTailscaleService' -v ./gcp/ && go test -count=1 ./gcp/
proof.observed: PASS. The Service's recorded inputs are name=svc:example-dispatch, ports=[tcp:443] and comment only: the property map holds no tags key at all. TestDispatchFrontDoorPodHostsTheTailscaleService passes unchanged, so the nodes still advertise the component's tags, and the whole gcp package passes, so the resolver still requires at least one tag (refuseDispatchTailnetGroup).
proof.negativeControl: TestDispatchDeclaresItsTailscaleService on the same unpacked starting tree FAILs: `resource.PropertyMap{"comment":..., "name":..., "ports":..., "tags":{V:"tag:example-dispatch"}} should not contain "tags"`.

proof.criterion: A3. The module is clean under the checks the envoy-infra-go job of .github/workflows/ci.yaml runs.
proof.surface: The same three commands in the Legion pod, from packages/envoy/infra.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy/infra && test -z "$(gofmt -l .)" && go vet -tags pulumilive,natslive ./... && go test ./...
proof.observed: gofmt clean; vet ok; every package ok, gcp included (110.143s). The pod carries no mkfs.ext4, blkid or blockdev, which gcp/data_disk_test.go fails without rather than skipping, so e2fsprogs 1.47.2 and util-linux 2.41.5 were unpacked from their Debian trixie packages into $TMPDIR/tools on the issue's volume and put on PATH and LD_LIBRARY_PATH for the run; nothing was installed into the image.
proof.negativeControl: Before those two packages were unpacked, the same `go test ./...` failed with `--- FAIL: TestARefusedDataDiskIsNeverFormattedOnALaterBoot ... these tests need mkfs.ext4 on this machine`, which is how that suite reports a missing tool rather than passing it over.

proof.criterion: A4. The plugin the release ships builds from the branch.
proof.surface: The plugin binary pulumi-resource-envoy-infra, the artifact the release's archives carry.
proof.negativeControl: The same build of the unpacked starting tree's module is the control for the compile; the build's own failure mode was seen earlier in this phase, when `go vet ./gcp/` refused the tree at `vet: gcp/dispatch_test.go:1408:24: undefined: bindingType` after a half-applied rename, and the build was not attempted until vet was clean.

proof.criterion: A5. The documents state the new contract.
proof.surface: packages/envoy/infra/README.md, the operator document a consumer reads before it moves its pin.
proof.command: grep -rn tags packages/envoy/infra/README.md packages/envoy/infra/docs/ | grep -i service
proof.observed: No sentence gives the Tailscale Service the component's tags. The resource table row, the declaration paragraph and the move checklist each read `no tags` and say why; the tailnet-policy paragraph and the checklist's step 1 now offer only the grant `dst: ["svc:<hostname>"]` with `ip: ["443"]` and say plainly that a grant whose dst names tags does not reach the Service; the adoption paragraph no longer claims the apply overwrites the Service's tags. The remaining hits are about the hosts' own tags, which are unchanged: the tailnet entry of gcp:NatsHub, the auth key minted with tags, and docs/nats-hub.md.
proof.negativeControl: The same grep over the starting tree returns the four sentences this change removes, among them `since the Service carries the same tags the front door's nodes do` and `overwrites its comment, its ports and its tags`.

filesChanged: packages/envoy/infra/gcp/dispatch_frontdoor.go: the RoleBinding's roleRef.name is built from the Role's ID, as agent-infra's shared/rbac ref does, and the Tailscale Service's ServiceArgs carries no Tags; both carry the comment that says why.

packages/envoy/infra/gcp/dispatch_test.go: TestDispatchFrontDoorBindingWaitsForItsRoleOnPreview reads both surfaces on a preview and on an apply; TestDispatchDeclaresItsTailscaleService asserts the Service's inputs hold no tags key; runDispatchOnMocks is split out of runDispatchWithProviders; the RBAC type tokens moved to the file's const block.

packages/envoy/infra/gcp/dispatch_construct_test.go: dispatchConstructProviders and constructDispatchOnMocks, which constructs through the plugin on mocks the caller owns and takes its dry run from Mocks.Preview.

packages/envoy/infra/internal/pulumitest/mocks.go: Mocks.Preview, which makes Run a dry run and answers a create with no ID, so a resource's ID and every output built on it is unknown (carried from sjawhar/legion#2661).
packages/envoy/infra/README.md: the five places that stated the old contract.
packages/envoy/.changes/unreleased/pr2668-Fixed-20261102-074520.yaml: the changelog fragment, which names the behaviour change for a tailnet policy.
trickyParts: The Construct surface needed mocks the test owns, since Mocks.Preview must be set before the program runs and the existing constructDispatch helpers allocate their own. constructDispatchOnMocks takes them and reads its dry run from m.Preview, so the engine's DryRun and the mocks' create answer cannot disagree.

The plugin surface refuses dispatchConstructInputs() alone (`tailnetAuthKey is required`), so the case uses dispatchConstructBaseInputs(), which sets the four Inputs a consumer takes from its own resources.

The preview assertion accepts null as well as computed: the mock monitor unmarshals a registration's inputs without keeping unknowns, so an unknown roleRef.name arrives as null. The negative control is what shows the assertion has teeth, since the old code puts the literal string there on both surfaces.

sjawhar/legion#2661 could not be retargeted, since GitHub cannot move an open pull request's head branch, so its commit was carried onto legion/INFRA-992 with the credit in the message, and #2661 was closed with a comment naming sjawhar/legion#2668. Its branch fix/envoy-infra-frontdoor-roleref was left in place.

The branch had moved under this phase: `legion handoffs import` had pushed 5b85da2d67b03f6ac276996597ae085208f7dfc1 onto legion/INFRA-992, removing .legion/INFRA-992/plan.json. The phase's own commits, none of them pushed yet, were rebased onto it, so the push is a fast-forward and nothing pushed was rewritten. previousHandoff is empty because no commit on this branch has ever changed .legion/INFRA-992/implement.json.
deviations: The simplify pass's three reviewers each proposed replacing `pulumi.All(role.ID(), role.Metadata.Name().Elem()).ApplyT(func(v []any) string { return v[1].(string) })` with `role.ID().ApplyT(func(pulumi.ID) string { return tlsName })`, which drops two output nodes and a type assertion. It was skipped, not applied: the spec and the plan name agent-infra's shared/rbac `ref` as the convention this change matches, and that function (theorem-labs/agent-infra shared/rbac/rbac.go:75-83, read as the implement App) is character for character the carried form. The replacement also names the Role by a local constant where the current form reads back what was declared. The cost it saves is three output nodes once per apply of a component that registers dozens of resources.

The same pass's proposal to collapse Mocks.Run's option guard to one unconditional `func(info *pulumi.RunInfo) { info.DryRun = m.Preview }` was skipped as not behaviour-preserving: RunInfo.DryRun is seeded from PULUMI_DRY_RUN, and the unconditional form would force it false where the current code leaves the environment's value alone.
discoveredComplexity: The pod's gh credential bundle stopped being refreshed at 2026-11-02T07:00:05Z (the mtime of both /var/run/legion/gh/sjawhar/hosts.yml and /var/run/legion/gh/theorem-labs/hosts.yml), and from about 08:00Z every GitHub call is refused: `gh: Bad credentials (HTTP 401)` and, for the push, `remote: Invalid username or token`. The daemon refreshes those directories every minute, so this is a pod-environment fault rather than anything this phase did. It was reported to the architect on its role topic.

This pod carries no mkfs.ext4, blkid or blockdev, so `go test ./...` of this module cannot be green in it as written: gcp/data_disk_test.go fails rather than skips without them (packages/envoy/infra/AGENTS.md says so deliberately). e2fsprogs 1.47.2 and util-linux 2.41.5 were unpacked from Debian trixie packages into $TMPDIR/tools on the issue's volume and put on PATH and LD_LIBRARY_PATH; a later role of this issue must do the same to reproduce the full run.
